messages:
zoe: FYI I tried the quickstart on a colleague's ThinkPad (Ubuntu, default snap store). Installed redwoodctl from snaps and the browser auth opened but redwoodctl said 'no profile found' after the flow. Anyone seen snap/flatpak weirdness with config paths?

ben: Snap/Flatpak usually keep app data under the sandbox (e.g. `/home/zoe/snap/redwoodctl/current/.config/redwood`) which our CLI doesn't check by default. We only look at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood` and `~/.config/redwood`.

zoe: I found token.json in the snap path but the CLI didn't pick it up. Symlinked it to `~/.config/redwood` and auth started working. But this seems bad for first-run UX.

priya: We have three short-term fixes: (1) document the symlink/headless token flow, (2) add `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR` env var + `--config-dir` flag so installs with nonstandard homes can point to the right dir, (3) add a snap/flatpak detection fallback to check `$SNAP_USER_DATA` / `FLATPAK_SANDBOX_DIR`.

ben: Agreed. Also suggest adding an interactive `--device` flow for constrained installs so users don't need localhost callbacks inside a sandbox. Many CLIs do this and it's friendly for AppImage/Flatpak.

zoe: For local testing I ran into another issue: infra mounts `/etc/redwood/profiles.yaml` in our dev VM with a default 'staging' profile. My `~/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml` should override it but local-run used the system one. I had to pass `--config /home/zoe/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml` to force my override.

priya: That's a bug in merge precedence. We intended user config to take priority over system defaults. We should (A) prefer XDG ~/.config over /etc, (B) add `profiles inspect <name>` to show which file won, and (C) emit a warning when a profile name is shadowed.

ben: Low-risk UX: print a small diagnostic on startup when multiple profile sources exist, like `Found profile 'staging' in /etc/redwood and ~/.config/redwood — using ~/.config/redwood`. That would save a lot of confusion.

packaging-bot: NOTE: opened GH issue #798 (packaging/devex: support sandbox config discovery + add --config-dir and device auth flow).

zoe: Workaround snippets I left for the teammate:```bash
# symlink for snap installs
mkdir -p ~/.config
ln -s /home/zoe/snap/redwoodctl/current/.config/redwood ~/.config/redwood
# headless token (if you exported token from dashboard)
redwoodctl auth login --headless --token-file ~/.config/redwood/token.json
# explicit config for local-run
redwoodctl local-run --config ~/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml --profile staging
```

priya: I'll draft a docs patch with these snippets and a short explanation about sandboxed packages. I'll also queue a small CLI PR to add `--config-dir` and `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR` (easy) and a follow-up to add device auth.

zoe: Happy to validate flags and docs. Thanks :thumbsup:
thread_text: Installed redwoodctl from snap on Ubuntu; browser auth finished but CLI reported 'no profile found' and local-run picked wrong profiles.
